description: Brown-and-white directional sign on twin posts, pointing to a temple, waterfall or national park.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Pair of slim galvanised posts carrying one wide rectangular flat board near the top, board face dark chocolate brown with a thin white border inset from the edge, white lettering reading the Thai line น้ำตกเอราวัณ above a smaller roman line reading ERAWAN WATERFALL, a white arrow pointing right at the end of the lettering, board mounted square across both posts Materials: Dark brown enamel dulled and chalky on the sun-facing side, white border paint flaking, galvanised posts with rust at the ground line, dirt streaking down the board face.

Legend: this object is a SIGN, and its printed legend is part of the object, not an annotation on the photograph. Render every letter, numeral, pictogram, arrow and coloured band described above, exactly as described and nothing more. Thai script must be rendered as Thai script with correct glyph shapes, above the roman line where both are described. Lettering and pictograms lie flat on the sign face, sharp, high-contrast and correctly proportioned, and the face must stay legible despite the camera angle. Do not leave the face blank, do not substitute lorem or invented wording, and do not add any text that was not described.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no drop shadow, and no border around the photograph itself.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: Two-component twin-post directional sign built to the declared 1.200 x 2.400 m. 580 triangles of 800, 2 draw calls of 2, 2 materials of 3, 2 unique geometries of 3, one texture. The passes were worked as ONE build with the deterministic gates run once over the finished prop rather than per pass; the per-pass content is real but the per-pass evidence is not, and that is stated rather than implied. Two splits were refused and both are recorded where someone tempted to make them will read them: the two legs are merged into ONE buffer rather than given a component each, which is the whole reason this prop fits two draw calls; and the wide painted frame is a printed region of the board's face rather than a modelled solid. The third material and third geometry were both available and neither was spent.

featureReviews.evidence: A 20-point rounded-rect extrusion at 1.2 x 0.62 m with a 12 mm radius - near-square corners, because the reference shows a framed board with sharp mitred corners rather than the design radii the informatory plates carry. Held at 0.86 because the board height is the lowest-confidence dimension in the spec: it comes from the Meshy proxy's band extent scaled against the declared width, not from a measurement of the image.

Two 48 mm round tubes at x = -0.405 and +0.405, merged into ONE BufferGeometry. Built as a genuine REFLECTION - the lateral axis negated and nothing else - rather than by rotating, so the chirality rule holds even though both tubes are surfaces of revolution and the distinction cannot show here. 440 of the prop's 580 triangles are in this component, which is right: a round section read as a polygon is the one defect a viewer notices on a tube, and there are two of them.

Wide painted frame, Thai place name, Latin transliteration and the direction arrow all ride ONE atlas on ONE material along with the weathered back. The arrow points RIGHT and that is chiral - an arrow the other way sends traffic the wrong way - and the front-cap UV mapping preserves the sign so the atlas is not mirrored.

Roughness 0.72 and materialClass wood, matte where every sibling in this set is satin vinyl at 0.42 - this is the only prop of the eight whose panel is painted timber, and treating it as sheeting would have been the easy error. Brown #655851 is a warm NEUTRAL rather than a printed colour, measured over 7200 px. Held at 0.78 because the paint flaking off the frame's arrises is drawn as scattered rectangles, which reads correctly at prop distance but is graphic rather than organic at close range.

Ramp baked as vertex colours over 10 height segments per tube, no texture, shared across both legs because the reference weathers them identically. The clean value rests on 7497 of 7500 neutral pixels - the cleanest galvanising reading of the eight props, against the no-parking post's 186. A RAMP rather than a hard splash line, because the reference shows rust climbing both tubes over their lower third with no top edge.
